characterization_methods.key_findings: At 30% CR, equiaxed grains elongate along RD with numerous slip bands; in certain grains slip bands intersect (Figure 2b).
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Cross-sections ground and polished along RD, etched with hydrochloric acid (100 mL), alcohol (100 mL), and copper chloride (5 g) etchant.

characterization_methods.key_findings: CR 30% fracture shows a network of dimples that are smaller and more numerous than the undeformed condition, with less prominent deep voids (Figure 9b).

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: JSM7200F SEM equipped with an EBSD system
characterization_methods.key_findings: After 30% CR: copper {112}<111> texture component appears; LAGB proportion significantly increases to 89.4%; higher KAM values near prior grain boundaries; IPF map shows grains roughly equiaxed but subdivided into colour-banded subgrains.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Samples prepared by electrochemical polishing in an electrolyte containing perchlorate acid (5%) and acetic acid (95%) at 50 V for 30 s.
characterization_methods.purpose: Characterize texture, grain boundaries (HAGB/LAGB) and kernel average misorientation (KAM).

characterization_methods.key_findings: CR 30%: dark mottled dislocation substructure with intersecting dashed yellow lines outlining a Taylor lattice (Figure 3b).
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Samples mechanically ground to 60 μm slices, punched into Ф3 mm disks, and thinned using a Gatan 691 ion milling machine.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: D8 ADVANCE X-ray diffractometer with Cu-Kα radiation (wavelength λ = 0.15406 nm)
characterization_methods.key_findings: Single-phase austenitic structure, no deformation-induced martensitic transformation; CR 30% austenitic (220) peak FWHM = 0.686°; microstrain = 3.6 × 10^-3; dislocation density = 6.2 × 10^14 m^-2.
characterization_methods.purpose: Phase identification and peak broadening analysis (FWHM, microstrain, dislocation density).

analytical_models.equation_role: β_τ = Kλ/(D cosθ) + 4ε tanθ; total broadening from grain refinement plus microstrain.
analytical_models.model_note: Through fitting analysis, microstrain and dislocation density were obtained for rolled specimens.

analytical_models.equation_role: Calculate dislocation density from microstrain and grain size.
analytical_models.model_note: The number of corresponding dislocation density is calculated using the average grain size and microstrain.

computational_details.validation_against_experiment: The dislocation density trend from XRD calculation aligns with TEM observations (Figure 3).

defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: In certain grains, slip bands of different orientations intersect, indicating nonuniform plastic deformation at 30% CR; their interaction produces the Taylor lattice structure.

defect_interactions.interaction_type: LAGB formation / deformation concentration near grain boundaries
defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: Higher KAM values are seen near the prior grain boundaries after 30% CR, suggesting that deformation concentration first occurs near grain boundaries; the LAGB fraction reaches 89.4%.

interfaces.phase_evolution: Single-phase austenite is retained; no deformation-induced martensitic phase transformation occurs during CR.
interfaces.slip_behavior: Planar slip of dislocations is the primary deformation mechanism at low strain (30% CR), producing slip bands; no deformation twinning is reported at this stage.

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Plate-shaped specimens with thicknesses of 1.5, 2, 3.5, and 10 mm were excised from the center of the billet in alignment with the forging direction; prior to CR, all specimens underwent solution treatment at 1000 °C for 1 h and were water-quenched to room temperature.

Using an LG-300 two-high rolling mill; after cooling in liquid nitrogen, the specimen was rapidly removed for a single-pass rolling with a thickness reduction of about 2%, then promptly re-immersed in liquid nitrogen; steps repeated until the cumulative thickness reduction reached 30% (CR 30%).

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Tensile tests were conducted in a temperature-controlled environment using a universal tensile testing machine; microhardness was measured with a loading of 500 g and a dwelling time of 15 s (values averaged from at least 5 measurements).
measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: dog-bone-shaped tensile specimens with standard distance segment of 20 × 5 × 1 mm machined along RD

tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: An engineering stress–strain curve for CR 30% is included among five colour-coded curves in Figure 8a; its peak stress is higher than the undeformed condition and lower than the higher CR reductions.

phases_present.morphology: elongated grains along RD with numerous slip bands in grain interiors

structures.overall_structure: Single-phase austenitic (FCC) structure retained; equiaxed austenite grains elongate along RD with numerous slip bands in grain interiors; slip bands intersect in certain grains; a substantial rise in dislocation density gives rise to Taylor lattice structure; no deformation-induced martensitic transformation.

unmapped_findings: SFE of this steel: 72 mJ m^-2 at room temperature and 51 mJ m^-2 at cryogenic temperature (block b0044); the cryogenic SFE is still higher than the ~20–40 mJ m^-2 range typically associated with twinning plasticity, but restraint of dislocation motion at low temperatures and accumulated dislocations promote deformation twinning at moderate strains.

Short-range order (SRO) clusters or κ-carbides, facilitated by the high Al and C content, can soften slip planes and facilitate planar slip (block b0043) — relevant to the 30% CR planar-slip mechanism.
